_README: Muscles of the male right forearm the cryosection photographs do not separate (vhm_forearm_muscles_from_cryo.py): each compartment is the union of its members' watershed regions and is mapped to null. Decided from the run's report (boundary_support: within-compartment boundary on a pale line, ridge ratio >= 1.8, at < 70 % of shared levels), 2026-09-14.

radial_flexor_compartment.note: PT/FPL split followed a pale line at 63 % of 27 shared levels and FCR/FPL at 66 % of 35; PT's region (7 cm3) is far too small for the muscle and FCR's (70 cm3) far too large, i.e. the line between them is not the PT/FCR/FPL septum. Kept together (105 cm3). Q106 (2026-09-21) tried a Q100-style position-rule split instead of the photograph line (distance to his CT radius surface, nearest-anchor and threshold-sweep variants, gated by MARKER_RULES' own f-windows): PT stayed 5-14 cm3 and FCR 68-80 cm3 across the whole sweep, i.e. the SAME implausible split the photograph watershed found, not fixed by moving the boundary. DECLINED -- the defect looks like a wrong region (FCR's definition absorbing PT/FPL territory), which a boundary-placement rule cannot repair; not shipped.

mobile_wad_compartment.note: BR/ECRL on a pale line at 68 % of 65 shared levels, ECRL/ECRB at 68 % of 62: the weakest extensor boundaries. The BR region (163 cm3) also holds the brachialis and biceps at the elbow levels (the position rules have no marker for them), so the compartment (264 cm3) is the anterolateral mass, not the three muscles alone. Q106 (2026-09-21) tried a Q100-style position-rule split (distance to his CT radius surface, MARKER_RULES' own e-offsets as anchors, gated by their f-windows): BR came out at 191 cm3 (textbook ~20-30 cm3 for this muscle), and per-level accounting shows the excess is spread through roughly the first 55 % of the segment, not concentrated in a few proximal levels that could be cut off by a level cutoff -- so the elbow contamination this compartment's own note already flags is not a boundary problem a position rule can fix here. DECLINED, per this task's own instruction not to force it; not shipped.

extensor_digitorum_supinator_anconeus_co.note: Anconeus/supinator on a pale line at only 44 % of 16 shared levels and ED/anconeus at 44 % of 9; the anconeus region (1.9 cm3) is too small to be the muscle, so ED, whose other boundaries hold (72-100 %), is kept with the two proximal muscles (49 cm3) rather than shipped with a border that does not run on a septum. Q106 (2026-09-21) tried a Q100-style position-rule split (scripts/cryo/vhm_split_forearm_extensor_compartment.py, kept committed as a documented attempt, not applied): level fraction + distance to his CT radius/ulna surface gave good mesh connectivity (98.7-100 % one component each) and plausible relative volumes (ED 36.0 / supinator 8.3 / anconeus 4.3 cm3, the right order and each larger/more plausible than the raw watershed's own attempt). DECLINED anyway: checking the split against his own CT skin surface (data/ct_sources/task_outputs/vhm_skin_ct.nii.gz, the same check clip_arm_to_skin.py uses for his arm muscles) found the WHOLE compartment's outside-skin fraction rises smoothly from 0 % in the segment's distal 60 % to ~22 % at its most proximal level -- a pre-existing registration gradient in the already-shipped volume, not introduced by this split. Anconeus (f<=0.12) and supinator (f<=0.28) sit almost entirely in that poorly-registered band by real anatomical position, so anconeus comes out 100 % outside his skin surface and supinator 72-82 %, in every variant tried, even after the same erosion-margin clip used for the arm. Not a boundary-placement problem a position rule can fix; would need the proximal segment's photograph-to-CT registration re-derived, out of scope here.
